review: 1:2 וְהוּא בַעֲדֵנוּ מֵת — 'and He died for us'; the Arabic وَهُوَ عَنَّا قَدْ قَضَى uses قَضَى ('decreed/died'), and Hebrew states the death plainly because the next line quotes Rom 8:31.
1:3–1:4 מִי אֵפוֹא נִירָא / וּבוֹ הִשַּׂגְנוּ רָצוֹן — Romans 8:31 and 5:2; the Arabic يَا تُرَى مِمَّنْ نَخَافُ is the same rhetorical question.
5:1–5:2 קָרָא לָנוּ בְּמַחֲשָׁבָה — 'He called us by purpose', for حَسْبَ قَصْدٍ; the noun מַחֲשָׁבָה is used in the sense of counsel/plan, as in Ps 33:11.
5:4 כְּצַלְמוֹ מְשַׁקֵּף — 'mirroring His image'; the hiph'il of שקף is the biblical verb for looking down/reflecting (Ps 85:12), and it covers the Arabic مُشْبِهًا صُورَتَهُ.
6:1 הִנֵּה בְיָד בָּרוּר נִמְלֹךְ — 'surely we shall reign'; the Arabic إِنَّنَا حَتْمًا سَنَمْلِك is 2 Tim 2:12, and בְּיָד בָּרוּר ('with a clear hand') supplies the certainty the metre needs.
